articles.title: World News in Brief: Winter aid for Gaza, West Bank; Haiti food production; migrant deaths at sea; human rights funding
articles.summary: The UN Children’s Fund (UNICEF) is seeking to raise $97.5 million to protect 540,000 children and their families in Gaza and the West Bank from harsh winter conditions in the coming months.
articles.content:
Nearly 84 per cent of Gaza’s population – more than 1.76 million people – live in overcrowded displacement sites or damaged shelters, leaving families vulnerable to freezing temperatures, heavy rain and flooding.

At least 11 children, including infants, in the Gaza Strip were reported to have died from hypothermia last winter.

Tweet URL

In the West Bank, violence, displacement, movement restrictions and a deepening financial crisis are further limiting vulnerable families’ ability to cope with winter shocks, UNICEF wrote in a press release.

The funding would allow UNICEF to provide more warm clothing, thermal blankets, digital cash assistance, emergency shelter reinforcements and tents. The agency will also work with partners to reduce flood and disease risks.

UNICEF is urging donors to provide flexible, timely funding so it can pre-position supplies before winter arrives.

Meanwhile, UN Humanitarian Coordinator for the Occupied Palestinian Territory Ramiz Alakbarov announced on Thursday that the UN’s aid agency (OCHA) will allocate $2 million to power health facilities in Gaza for four months.

FAO plants seeds of hope in Haiti

In the hills and plains of Haiti’s hardest-hit regions, families who have gone months eating whatever they could find are once again planting their own fields.

Emergency support from the UN’s Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) is reaching 13,000 vulnerable households – roughly 65,000 people – across 10 municipalities in Artibonite, Centre and Ouest, helping them restore local food production amid one of the world’s most severe hunger crises.

More than half of Haiti’s population faces acute food insecurity, driven by violence, economic collapse, broken supply chains and repeated climate shocks, according to FAO.

For many rural families, the FAO programme – funded with more than $16 million through a UN-managed pooled funding mechanism – is arriving at a critical moment. FAO said it will deliver more than 205 tonnes of crop and vegetable seeds and more than 160,000 small livestock to 326,000 vulnerable people.

“In humanitarian crises, emergency food production is a life-saving intervention that empowers vulnerable households to quickly produce food and reduce reliance on importations and repeated humanitarian assistance,” FAO Representative in Haiti Pierre Vauthier said.

Built by Haitians, for Haitians

Local communities are shaping the response by helping FAO identify those most in need and decide what support will help most.

“This emergency food production campaign demonstrates that investing in local capacities is one of the most effective ways to respond to the food crisis,” Mr. Vauthier said. “Implemented by Haitians for Haitians, it enables vulnerable households to rapidly produce their own nutritious food.”

A second phase will bring ducks, poultry, guinea fowls, rabbits and goats to more than 29,394 households, offering families a source of protein and a measure of self-sufficiency at the same time.

Mediterranean migrant deaths rise this year

Arrivals to Europe by sea have fallen sharply this year, but deaths and disappearances along Mediterranean migration routes have increased, according to new data from the UN’s International Organization for Migration (IOM).

Nearly 60,000 migrants and refugees have reached Europe by sea so far in 2026, a 39 per cent decline from the same period last year. But at least 2,292 people have died or gone missing attempting the journey, up from 1,999 by the same time last year.

Arrivals in Italy from the Central Mediterranean route fell 55 per cent from 48,231 to 21,393, while deaths rose from 844 to 996.

Increasingly desperate

On the Eastern Mediterranean route, arrivals in Greece fell by about 5,000, while deaths increased by 133. Spain also recorded fewer arrivals but maintained a similar number of deaths.

IOM Director General Amy Pope said the figures show migrants are taking increasingly dangerous journeys and called for greater international cooperation, including expanded safe and regular pathways.

The figures cover verified incidents through 15 September. IOM warned the true death toll is likely higher.

‘Entire’ human rights monitoring system risks crumbling: Türk

Tweet URL

The protection of human rights is a core founding principle of the UN, but a key part of this mission is on the verge of collapse because of funding cuts, High Commissioner for Human Rights Volker Türk told the Human Rights Council on Thursday.

“Today, I am very concerned that the entire human rights treaty body system is at risk of crumbling,” Mr. Türk said.

He cited funding cuts necessitating staff reductions, which has increased delays in processing requests for help, as well as the declining participation of Member States in reporting alleged violations.

Ten treaty body committees are based in Geneva, made up of independent experts who assess countries’ progress in implementing international accords or conventions, including on the elimination of racial discrimination and the promotion of children’s rights.

This is not the first time the High Commissioner has warned about a serious lack of funding for human rights work.

His appeal to Member States to fulfill their international obligations comes ahead of the publication of a report on the treaty body system by UN Secretary-General António Guterres next week during the UN General Assembly’s high-level week.

articles.personality_title: UN steps up winter aid for Gaza and food support in Haiti amid rising migrant risks
articles.personality_presentation:
**Context** – Many people in Gaza and the West Bank live in crowded or damaged shelters, making them vulnerable to cold winter weather. In Haiti, violence and economic problems have caused a severe food crisis. At the same time, migrant deaths in the Mediterranean Sea are increasing, and funding for human rights monitoring is shrinking.

**What happened** – UNICEF is asking for $97.5 million to help 540,000 children and families in Gaza and the West Bank stay safe this winter. This money will buy warm clothes, blankets, and tents, and help prepare for floods and diseases. The UN’s aid agency will give $2 million to keep health centers in Gaza running for four months. Meanwhile, the UN’s Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) is supporting 13,000 Haitian families to plant crops and raise animals, helping them grow their own food again. However, the International Organization for Migration (IOM) reports more migrant deaths in the Mediterranean despite fewer arrivals. Finally, the UN’s human rights monitoring system is at risk because of funding cuts.

**Impact** – The UNICEF winter aid could prevent deaths from cold weather like last winter, when at least 11 children died from hypothermia in Gaza. FAO’s support helps Haitian families move from relying on emergency food aid to growing and raising their own food, which improves their independence and nutrition. The rising migrant deaths highlight the dangers people face while seeking safety. The warning about human rights funding shows that important work protecting people’s rights may be weakened if support is not restored.

**What's next step** – UNICEF urges donors to provide money soon so supplies can arrive before winter. FAO will continue its program with a second phase, giving more animals to Haitian families. IOM calls for better international cooperation to create safer migration routes. The UN Secretary-General will release a report on the human rights treaty system, aiming to encourage governments to increase funding and participation.

**One-sentence takeaway** – UNICEF and FAO are delivering vital aid to protect vulnerable families in Gaza, the West Bank, and Haiti, while the UN highlights urgent needs to improve migrant safety and sustain human rights monitoring.
articles.personality_title_fr: L’ONU intensifie l’aide hivernale à Gaza et le soutien alimentaire en Haïti face aux risques migratoires croissants
articles.personality_presentation_fr:
**Contexte** – De nombreuses personnes à Gaza et en Cisjordanie vivent dans des abris surpeuplés ou endommagés, ce qui les rend vulnérables au froid hivernal. En Haïti, la violence et les problèmes économiques ont provoqué une grave crise alimentaire. Parallèlement, les décès de migrants en mer Méditerranée augmentent, et le financement du suivi des droits humains diminue.

**Ce qui s’est passé** – UNICEF demande 97,5 millions de dollars pour aider 540 000 enfants et familles à Gaza et en Cisjordanie à rester en sécurité cet hiver. Cet argent servira à acheter des vêtements chauds, des couvertures et des tentes, et à préparer la lutte contre les inondations et les maladies. L’agence d’aide de l’ONU alloue 2 millions de dollars pour maintenir en fonctionnement les centres de santé à Gaza pendant quatre mois. Par ailleurs, l’Organisation des Nations Unies pour l’alimentation et l’agriculture (FAO) soutient 13 000 familles haïtiennes pour qu’elles replante leurs champs et élèvent des animaux, les aidant à produire leur propre nourriture. Cependant, l’Organisation internationale pour les migrations (OIM) rapporte une augmentation des décès de migrants en Méditerranée malgré la baisse des arrivées. Enfin, le système de surveillance des droits humains de l’ONU est menacé par des coupes budgétaires.

**Impact** – L’aide hivernale d’UNICEF pourrait éviter des décès dus au froid, comme l’hiver dernier où au moins 11 enfants sont morts d’hypothermie à Gaza. Le soutien de la FAO aide les familles haïtiennes à passer de l’aide alimentaire d’urgence à la production autonome, améliorant leur indépendance et leur nutrition. La hausse des décès de migrants souligne les dangers auxquels ils sont exposés. L’alerte sur le financement des droits humains montre que ce travail essentiel pourrait être affaibli sans un soutien renforcé.

**Prochaine étape** – UNICEF appelle les donateurs à fournir rapidement des fonds pour que les fournitures arrivent avant l’hiver. La FAO poursuivra son programme avec une deuxième phase, distribuant plus d’animaux aux familles haïtiennes. L’OIM demande une meilleure coopération internationale pour créer des voies migratoires plus sûres. Le Secrétaire général de l’ONU publiera un rapport sur le système des traités des droits humains, visant à encourager les États à augmenter le financement et la participation.

**En une phrase** – UNICEF et FAO fournissent une aide essentielle pour protéger les familles vulnérables à Gaza, en Cisjordanie et en Haïti, tandis que l’ONU souligne les besoins urgents pour améliorer la sécurité des migrants et maintenir la surveillance des droits humains.
articles.personality_title_es: La ONU refuerza ayuda invernal en Gaza y apoyo alimentario en Haití ante crecientes riesgos migratorios
articles.personality_presentation_es:
**Contexto** – Muchas personas en Gaza y Cisjordania viven en refugios hacinados o dañados, lo que las hace vulnerables al frío del invierno. En Haití, la violencia y los problemas económicos han causado una grave crisis alimentaria. Al mismo tiempo, aumentan las muertes de migrantes en el mar Mediterráneo y se reduce el financiamiento para la supervisión de los derechos humanos.

**Qué pasó** – UNICEF está pidiendo 97,5 millones de dólares para ayudar a 540,000 niños y familias en Gaza y Cisjordania a mantenerse seguros durante el invierno. Este dinero se usará para comprar ropa abrigada, mantas y tiendas, y para prepararse contra inundaciones y enfermedades. La agencia de ayuda de la ONU asignó 2 millones de dólares para mantener en funcionamiento centros de salud en Gaza durante cuatro meses. Mientras tanto, la Organización de las Naciones Unidas para la Alimentación y la Agricultura (FAO) está apoyando a 13,000 familias haitianas para que planten cultivos y críen animales, ayudándolas a producir su propia comida. Sin embargo, la Organización Internacional para las Migraciones (OIM) informa que las muertes de migrantes aumentan a pesar de que las llegadas disminuyen. Por último, el sistema de monitoreo de derechos humanos de la ONU está en riesgo por recortes presupuestarios.

**Impacto** – La ayuda invernal de UNICEF podría evitar muertes por frío, como el invierno pasado cuando al menos 11 niños murieron por hipotermia en Gaza. El apoyo de FAO ayuda a las familias haitianas a pasar de depender de la ayuda alimentaria a producir su propia comida, mejorando su independencia y nutrición. El aumento de muertes de migrantes muestra los peligros que enfrentan. La advertencia sobre el financiamiento de derechos humanos indica que este trabajo importante podría debilitarse sin más apoyo.

**Próximo paso** – UNICEF insta a los donantes a proporcionar fondos pronto para que los suministros lleguen antes del invierno. FAO continuará su programa con una segunda fase, entregando más animales a las familias haitianas. OIM pide mayor cooperación internacional para crear rutas migratorias más seguras. El Secretario General de la ONU publicará un informe sobre el sistema de tratados de derechos humanos para alentar a los países a aumentar el financiamiento y la participación.

**Una frase clave** – UNICEF y FAO están entregando ayuda vital para proteger a familias vulnerables en Gaza, Cisjordania y Haití, mientras la ONU destaca la necesidad urgente de mejorar la seguridad migratoria y mantener la supervisión de los derechos humanos.
